[2023 fall ms math-stat — problem 6]

$X$ has density $f(x\mid\theta) = 2x/\theta^2$ for $0 < x \le \theta$ (0 otherwise), with $\theta \in (0,1)$. (1) Find $\mathbb{E}_\theta\{X\}$ and $\operatorname{Var}_\theta\{X\}$. (2) Find the MLE of $\theta$. (3) Find an unbiased estimator of $\theta(1-\theta)$.

response.text:
For one observation \(X\) with density

\[
f(x\mid \theta)=\frac{2x}{\theta^2},\qquad 0<x\le \theta,\quad 0<\theta<1,
\]

we proceed as follows.

## (1) Mean and variance

\[
\mathbb E_\theta[X]
=\int_0^\theta x\frac{2x}{\theta^2}\,dx
=\frac{2}{\theta^2}\int_0^\theta x^2\,dx
=\frac{2}{\theta^2}\cdot \frac{\theta^3}{3}
=\frac{2\theta}{3}.
\]

Also,

\[
\mathbb E_\theta[X^2]
=\int_0^\theta x^2\frac{2x}{\theta^2}\,dx
=\frac{2}{\theta^2}\int_0^\theta x^3\,dx
=\frac{2}{\theta^2}\cdot \frac{\theta^4}{4}
=\frac{\theta^2}{2}.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\operatorname{Var}_\theta(X)
=\mathbb E_\theta[X^2]-\{\mathbb E_\theta[X]\}^2
=\frac{\theta^2}{2}-\left(\frac{2\theta}{3}\right)^2
=\frac{\theta^2}{2}-\frac{4\theta^2}{9}
=\frac{\theta^2}{18}.
\]

So

\[
\boxed{\mathbb E_\theta[X]=\frac{2\theta}{3}},\qquad
\boxed{\operatorname{Var}_\theta(X)=\frac{\theta^2}{18}}.
\]

---

## (2) MLE of \(\theta\)

For an observed value \(x\), the likelihood is

\[
L(\theta\mid x)=\frac{2x}{\theta^2}\mathbf 1_{\{x\le \theta<1\}}.
\]

For fixed \(x\), this is proportional to \(\theta^{-2}\) over the allowable region \(\theta\ge x\). Since \(\theta^{-2}\) is strictly decreasing in \(\theta\), the likelihood is maximized by the smallest allowable value of \(\theta\), namely \(\theta=x\).

Thus the MLE is

\[
\boxed{\widehat\theta_{\text{MLE}}=X}.
\]

If instead one has an i.i.d. sample \(X_1,\dots,X_n\), then the same argument gives

\[
\boxed{\widehat\theta_{\text{MLE}}=X_{(n)}=\max\{X_1,\dots,X_n\}}.
\]

---

## (3) An unbiased estimator of \(\theta(1-\theta)\)

We look for an estimator of the form

\[
aX+bX^2.
\]

Using the moments found above,

\[
\mathbb E_\theta[aX+bX^2]
=a\frac{2\theta}{3}+b\frac{\theta^2}{2}.
\]

We want this to equal

\[
\theta(1-\theta)=\theta-\theta^2
\]

for all \(0<\theta<1\). Matching coefficients gives

\[
\frac{2a}{3}=1,\qquad \frac{b}{2}=-1.
\]

Hence

\[
a=\frac32,\qquad b=-2.
\]

Therefore,

\[
T(X)=\frac32 X-2X^2
\]

is unbiased for \(\theta(1-\theta)\), since

\[
\mathbb E_\theta\left[\frac32 X-2X^2\right]
=\frac32\cdot \frac{2\theta}{3}-2\cdot \frac{\theta^2}{2}
=\theta-\theta^2
=\theta(1-\theta).
\]

Thus an unbiased estimator is

\[
\boxed{\frac32 X-2X^2}.
\]
